sources.entry: TDD Guard by Nizar Selander - A hooks-driven system that monitors file operations in real-time and blocks changes that violate TDD principles.

summary.one_liner: TDD Guard is a Claude Code plugin that enforces Test-Driven Development by blocking agent actions that skip failing tests or over-implement.
summary.what_it_does: TDD Guard hooks into Claude Code to watch file operations and block changes that violate TDD principles. It requires a failing test before implementation is written, and it aims to stop code beyond what the current tests call for. It can enforce refactoring using the project's lint rules. Validation rules are customizable through custom instructions, and the validation model can be chosen for speed or capability. Enforcement can be toggled on and off during a session. The README says the setup command configures a test reporter for the project.
use_cases: enforce test-first development with an AI coding agent
stop Claude Code from writing implementation before tests
prevent over-implementation beyond current test requirements
automate refactoring checks using lint rules
guard TDD workflow in Vitest, Jest, or pytest projects
how_to_run: In Claude Code, run: /plugin marketplace add nizos/tdd-guard
Restart the terminal session or IDE extension if the setup skill does not appear
notable: Blocks agent actions in real time through Claude Code hooks
Supports many test frameworks through per-language contributors
Lint integration for automated refactoring enforcement
Session toggle to turn enforcement on or off mid-session
Successor project Probity covers Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot CLI without test reporters
caveats: The README says TDD Guard has been superseded by Probity, and new projects are advised to start there
Requires Node.js 22+ and a supported test framework
Hooks run with the user's permissions, so the README advises reviewing the source
keywords: keep ai agent honest about tests
stop ai writing code before tests
